source: Always be climbing the gear ladder: wood, then stone, then iron, then diamond. Whenever the materials for a better sword, pickaxe or piece of armour are in the bag, craft it immediately and wear it.
Better armour and a better weapon are the difference between surviving a fight and dying in one, so gear upgrades come before hoarding materials -- spend the iron and the diamonds, do not bank them.
Mine ore whenever it is in reach, working up from coal and iron to diamond, and keep a pickaxe good enough for what you are digging.
Light the tunnels, go back to the surface when hurt or out of air, and haul the ore and stone back to the base chests instead of carrying it all.
Stay alive above all else: get to air when drowning, run and eat when hurt, hold a weapon when something hostile is close, and sleep through the night in a bed.
Never let hunger become an emergency. Eat well before the hunger bar starts draining health, and go looking for food while there is still time to find it.
Keep a home base: gather wood, craft and place a room of chests, remember where it is, and use it to store surplus food, ore and building blocks.

Stay out of water you cannot see the bottom of. Getting to air when drowning is already a rule; this is the half that stops it happening -- only enter shallow, open water, never enclosed or underground water, and never swim far from shore.
Do not fight without a weapon in hand, and do not go back to where you last died until it is daylight and you are armed.

Run from what you cannot fight. Strays and the illager family shoot and charge from further away than you notice them, so put real distance between you and them rather than backing off a few blocks. Standing still is never the answer to a mob: mobs do not wander off because you waited, so never answer a mob by staying put.

Cold is a way to die here, not just weather. If you start freezing, that is a countdown: get out of the snow and under cover, or put something warm between you and it. Standing where you are does not warm you up.
Never walk off a drop of four blocks or more. Go around, or dig a staircase down -- falling is a way to die that nothing else in this policy can save you from.

Never approach a hostile mob, and never chase one. Nothing worth having is standing next to a zombie: the mobs come to you, so closing distance only ever buys damage, and doing it unarmed is how this bot has died most often. This goes double for what the goal loop does between rules -- searching for an entity, walking back to a death spot for dropped gear, or looting near a spawner is approaching, whatever it is called. Endermen are the sharpest case: neutral until looked at or struck, lethal after, and they follow you when they teleport.

A bed is the cheapest night there is: sleeping through the dark costs nothing and skips every shelter rule, so getting one is worth a detour long before it is urgent. It is three wool and three planks here, nothing exotic -- hunt sheep for the wool, craft it, and put it down somewhere sheltered. Do not spend an LLM turn asking how.
Keep out of the water rather than only climbing out of it. Wading is how this bot freezes, loses its path halfway across, and drowns; the shore is always the better route even when it is longer.

Be armed before you need to be. Crafting a weapon and drawing it are both free, and going into the dark without one is what most of this bot's deaths have had in common -- eleven of seventeen in one soak.

Never go back to where you died until it is daylight and you are holding a weapon. Whatever killed you is still there, your gear is next to it, and the bot has died five times at one spot in a single game-day doing exactly this.

A bed is only worth having where it is safe to sleep. Do not place one within reach of something hunting, and do not cross a killing field to reach one -- digging in for the night is better than a bed you die in.

When the pathfinder keeps failing from the same block, stop asking it. The route is not there; go somewhere else and try from a different place. Retrying in position is how whole game-days disappear into a single hole.
Build up a food surplus instead of eating hand to mouth. Harvest carrots, potatoes, beetroot and sweet berries whenever they are in reach, and hunt nearby animals when the meat supply is short.
Cook raw meat at a furnace before storing it, and bank the surplus in the base chests so there is always food to come home to.

Being unarmed is never a reason to stop feeding yourself. Foraging, baking, cooking and going out to look for food all happen whether or not there is a weapon in the bag -- an agent that cannot get wood must still be able to eat.

A base in a barren area starves you slowly. When no berry bushes, crops or animals live within reach of the base, ranging out to find them IS the job: explore until you find a berry patch, a herd, or ground fit for a farm, !rememberHere the spot, and haul the harvest home. If you ever hold seeds, till ground near water at the base and plant them -- a farm is the only food source that comes to you.

Remember the places that pay off. The moment a berry patch or the base chest is in sight, remember_here it under a fixed name ("berries", "pantry") -- finding it was the expensive part, and a remembered spot makes every later trip a free goto_place instead of another 128-block search or another LLM turn. Gate the remembering on "not place_known" so it happens once, and gate the walking on place_known so the rule stays quiet until there is somewhere to go.
goal: Stay alive indefinitely, keep a self-sustaining food surplus at your base, and work your way up the gear ladder from wood to stone to iron to diamond. Keep a bed and stocked chests, keep food, shelter and the best weapon and armour you have made between you and every way this world can end you. Actively farm, forage, hunt and remember productive spots, and mine coal, iron and diamond with a pickaxe good enough for the job, light what you dig, and haul the ore and harvest home to the base chests. Spend better gear the moment you can craft it -- wear it, do not bank it. Work the land within your exploration radius; your base stays where it is. Be at camp when night falls, and spend the night working the things camp is for rather than waiting in a hole for morning.

do.message:
YOU ARE FREEZING. The freeze meter is nearly full and it will start taking your health, then kill you -- you have died this way before. This is not something to wait out; standing still is what fills the meter.
Do one of these NOW, whichever is closest:
- If you are standing in powder snow, get OUT of it first -- !moveAway 8. It looks like a normal snow block and it is the fastest way to freeze.
- Get under cover and out of the weather: dig two blocks into the nearest hillside, or dig down two and put a block over your head. Being enclosed stops the snow reaching you.
- Put a heat source next to you: !placeHere torch, or a campfire if you have one. Then stay beside it, not merely near it.
- Leather armour stops freezing entirely. If you have leather, !craftRecipe leather_boots and the rest, and !equip them.
If none of that is possible where you stand, walk out of the snow: pick a direction and !moveAway 32, then look again. Any of these beats another second in the open.

do.message:
It is night and you have no bed, so you cannot sleep through it -- you have to survive it instead. Do NOT stand in the open. Dig two blocks into the nearest hillside, or straight down two, and cover the opening above you with dirt, cobblestone or planks. Place a torch inside so nothing spawns in with you.
READ THIS PART CAREFULLY, YOU HAVE GOT IT WRONG BEFORE. You have repeatedly walled yourself in on all sides and then been unable to travel at all for the rest of the night and the whole next day. Do not build a box around yourself. You need exactly enough cover to stop a mob reaching you and NOT ONE BLOCK MORE:
- Cover yourself with blocks YOU CAN BREAK -- dirt, planks, cobblestone. Never seal yourself behind anything you have no tool for.
- Do not place blocks on all four sides plus the roof. A two-deep hole with the entrance covered is enough.
- Before you settle, know which single block you will break to get out, and make sure it is one you can reach and break from where you are standing.
AT FIRST LIGHT, LEAVE. Break your way out and get back to work -- do not sit in the hole through the day. If you ever find that you cannot travel anywhere, the first thing to suspect is that you are still inside one of these shelters: break out sideways at your own feet level before trying to go anywhere.

do.message: You are carrying no food at all and there is nothing to forage or hunt within reach. Do not wait for hunger to force this. Go and look, and pick what suits the land you are actually standing in rather than what you wish were here. In a snowy pine forest that means sweet berry bushes and rabbits, not cows and wheat fields. Try in this order: !searchForBlock sweet_berry_bush 128 and !collectBlocks them -- berry bushes regrow, so a patch you find once is food forever, and !rememberHere it. Otherwise !searchForEntity for whatever animal lives here -- rabbit, sheep, chicken, cow, pig, fox -- and !attack it, then !smeltItem the raw meat if a furnace is in reach. Bare hands are enough for any of those; they do not fight back. They are not enough for anything that does, so if you are unarmed do not let a hunt turn into a fight. If you have string from spiders, 3 sticks and 2 string make a fishing_rod and any open water is then food you can stand still for. Finish one of these before starting anything else, and if a search says it could not travel at all, move somewhere else first -- searching again from a spot you cannot leave will not work.

rules.name: craft_diamond_armor
rules.description: The top of the ladder. Diamonds in the bag belong on your body, not in a chest. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: craft_diamond_weapon
rules.description: A diamond sword ends fights before they cost health. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: craft_iron_armor
rules.description: A full set of iron is what makes the night survivable. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: craft_iron_tools
rules.description: An iron sword and pickaxe: better fights, and the only way to reach diamond. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: craft_stone_gear
rules.description: The first real upgrade. Cobblestone is everywhere, so there is no excuse for wooden tools. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: craft_first_tools
rules.description: Nothing at all in hand: wooden tools now, better ones the moment stone shows up. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: wear_the_armor_you_have
rules.description: Armour in the bag protects nothing. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: hold_the_best_weapon
rules.description: Keep the upgrade in hand, not in the bag.

rules.name: go_get_the_next_tier
rules.description: Idle with a working pickaxe and no iron yet: the next tier is underground, not here.

rules.name: mine_diamond_ore
rules.description: Diamond first, always -- it is the rarest thing you will walk past.

rules.name: mine_iron_ore
rules.description: Iron is armour, tools and buckets. Take every vein you find.

rules.name: mine_coal_ore
rules.description: Coal is torches and furnace fuel, and torches are what keep the tunnel safe.

rules.name: keep_stone_stocked
rules.description: Cobblestone is furnaces, tools and a wall between you and whatever is down there.

rules.name: smelt_raw_ore
rules.description: Raw ore is dead weight until it goes through a furnace. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: make_torches_for_the_tunnel
rules.description: A dark tunnel spawns the mobs that kill you. Coal plus sticks fixes that. Named actions, not a prompt: the item is known exactly, so spending an LLM turn to ask for it bought nothing but cost and latency.

rules.name: go_find_ore
rules.description: Nothing worth mining in sight: go look for a vein rather than standing around.

rules.name: surface_when_hurt_underground
rules.description: Bleeding in a tunnel with no way out is how mining trips end. Climb out and eat. Gated on having food: with an empty bag the consume does nothing, so it re-fires every cooldown and cancels every other action.

rules.name: haul_ore_to_base
rules.description: Carry the ore home instead of losing the lot to one bad fall.
